characters.name: 조은
characters.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / new-pose character illustration. Produce ONE finished high-end 2D semi-real painterly Korean RPG Halloween character illustration, native 1024x1536 exact portrait 2:3. Image 1 is the previous Halloween costume and exact face/body/style reference, NOT a pose or weapon-geometry template. Image 2 is the original approved identity reference. Keep this same mature adult woman, exact facial identity, eye/nose/mouth/jaw relationships, natural hair, adult bust-waist-hip proportions and long natural legs. Keep her existing Halloween costume's fabric, colors and motifs. The user explicitly rejected the prior weapon handling and now requires a COMPLETELY NEW BODY POSE AND HAND GRIP. Plan a mechanically correct straight rigid weapon FIRST, then arrange the arms, wrists and fingers around it. Do not simply paste a new weapon into the old pose. Every hand has five anatomically coherent fingers and a natural thumb wrapped around the actual grip. Preserve the original premium painterly finish, natural continuous hair strands, soft face lighting, sophisticated garment and metal materials. No new words, rank, frame, UI, logo, watermark, signature, construction lines or annotations. Fully covered short skirt and graceful long legs, no underwear view or extreme low-angle framing. Identity, body shape, costume and art style must be retained while pose changes.
JOEUN / 조은. Preserve the aubergine fitted office blazer, white blouse, black tie with spider brooch, short tailored black pencil skirt with cobweb embroidery, pumpkin amethyst belt clasp and black ankle-strap heels. Exact same black hair and recognizable face. New body pose: a competent machine gunner's shouldered ready-to-aim stance, body turned toward the VIEWER'S RIGHT at a clear three-quarter side angle, feet uncrossed and planted shoulder-width apart, forward knee only slightly soft, back leg straight, weight centered. Head upright, eyes looking along the weapon toward the right, enough of her face visible above the rifle to recognize her. This is wholly different from the old crossed-leg low-ready office pose.
WEAPON AND HANDLING, TOP PRIORITY:
One reasonably scaled box-fed/light belt-fed machine gun held nearly HORIZONTAL at upper-chest/shoulder height. The buttpad is visibly and firmly seated against her RIGHT shoulder pocket. Right hand wraps the pistol grip immediately behind the trigger guard, wrist neutral; finger indexed naturally beside trigger guard. Left hand supports the underside of the front handguard, palm actually touching the gun, fingers wrapping naturally around its underside, left elbow BELOW the fore-end, both elbows in physically plausible positions. The gun cannot float away from shoulder or hands.
The gun runs across the frame toward viewer's RIGHT, flat side profile and minimal foreshortening. Keep full buttstock and full muzzle visible with generous margins. Choose one almost horizontal barrel axis with no more than a 5-degree rise. The longitudinal centers of buttstock attachment, rear receiver, chamber, front receiver, handguard, barrel tube and muzzle are COLLINEAR on that one ruler-straight axis. All top-rail segments form one continuous straight line parallel to the barrel; long external edges never kink at a joint or support hand. Straight tubular barrel extends coaxially from the receiver/handguard, straight muzzle attaches on exactly the same axis. Design this as ONE rigid coherent manufactured firearm, not separate pieces at different angles. The grip and ammo box hang below that straight body and cannot shift the central barrel axis.
Keep a graphite-and-silver Halloween bat-themed fantasy machine-gun skin with restrained violet core insets and a small ammunition box; simplify bulky ornament where it hides the clear straight form. No wings or curved plating masquerading as the barrel. No muzzle flash, motion blur, extra weapons or disconnected ammunition. Do not deform gun to meet old arm locations: fully redesign arm positions to fit this correct shouldered weapon.
Camera: level at upper chest, wider enough to fit full weapon, head and both feet. Character fills the portrait with readable face and long unchanged legs. Haunted executive salon with arched windows and dark violet Halloween details; desk shifted behind her so the new firing-ready silhouette is unobstructed. The weapon is a clean readable horizontal line above the waist, not a diagonally sagging low carry gun. No perspective excuse for bent geometry.
